rich_narrative.summary: The Islamic Center of Southern California faces significant operational efficiency limitations due to high overhead expenses and a low program expense ratio. In FY2024 filings, the organization reported a <cite id="3">Total Revenue of $2,134,893</cite>, but allocated a <cite id="1">Program expense ratio of 49.6%</cite>, leaving <cite id="1">nearly half of its funds directed toward administrative and support costs</cite>. This program spending level falls well below the <cite id="1">75% industry standard</cite> and the <cite id="1">peer program ratio median of 89.5%</cite>. Third-party evaluations reflect these structural challenges, as the center holds a <cite id="1">66/100 rating from Charity Navigator</cite>. Founded in <cite id="4">1952</cite>, the center provides local community services, including a <cite id="4">food pantry, Sunday school, and weekly lectures</cite>. The organization is <cite id="2">zakat-eligible</cite>, collecting funds for categories including the poor (<cite id="6">fuqara</cite>) and needy (<cite id="6">masakin</cite>). However, the absence of a documented theory of change and limited long-term outcome evaluations restrict its overall programmatic effectiveness.
